title: Hear the Sweet Spot: Tennis Impact Localization via Single-Channel Audio
evidence: Publisher abstract: single-channel audio, multi-expert multi-scale CNN, joint radial classification and position regression, noise augmentation. Full publisher page returned HTTP 429; detailed architecture/dataset claims were not verified here.

title: SmartDampener: An Open Source Platform for Sport Analytics in Tennis
evidence: Authors PDF, sections 5.3 and 6: separate coordinate SVR models. Uses IMU/string-mounted sensing; its errors are not directly comparable to handle-microphone radial MAE.

title: The sweet spots of a tennis racquet — Rod Cross
evidence: Hand/grip affects racket response; geometric centre, vibration node and centre of percussion are distinct concepts.

title: Tennis Racket Vibrations and Shock Transmission to the Wrist during Forehand Drive
evidence: Vibration modes, damping, velocity effects and relative low-frequency energy measurements.

title: Nested versus non-nested cross-validation
evidence: Keep parameter selection inside the training folds to reduce selection bias.

title: Kymatio scattering-transform user guide
evidence: Fixed wavelet filters and modulus operations reduce irrelevant variation; potential small-data representation. Full scattering was not tested in this pass.

title: MFCC documentation — librosa
evidence: Mel-spectral features and DCT representation; our HTK-mel implementation is explicit and not claimed identical to librosa default parameters.

title: Wavelet packet decomposition — MathWorks
evidence: Relative sub-band energies can form classification features.

title: HuberRegressor documentation
evidence: L2-regularized regression with reduced influence from large residuals; our fixed-delta IRLS variant is not claimed identical to sklearn.

title: SVR documentation
evidence: Epsilon-insensitive support-vector regression. The local research solver uses the dual QP, not libsvm.

title: SciPy SLSQP documentation
evidence: Constrained optimization for the local epsilon-SVR dual.
